summary: Partial reserved-capacity refund applied but hosted rate override charged on finalized invoice
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightLens reports that a partial refund for reserved GPU hours (requested 2026-03-05) was processed, but the finalized invoice (2026-03-08) contains a line where the reserved quantity is zeroed and the usage was billed at hosted (pay-as-you-go) rate rather than applying the prorated refunded reserved rate. Impact: BrightLens sees ~USD 3,600 unexpected increase on their monthly invoice; finance flagged the discrepancy and paused autopay. Environment: Dedicated subscription (monthly reserved pool) in prod-us-east, customer org id: org-brightlens-77. Observed behavior: 1) Refund transaction ID REF-20260305-77 shows partial refund of 320 reserved hours. 2) Hourly accumulator showed a mid-cycle swap from reserved->hosted for a narrow window during the refund application. 3) Finalized invoice shows a hosted-rate line for hours between 2026-03-05T23:00 and 2026-03-06T02:00 UTC. Steps to reproduce / trace: a) Reserve refund job ran 2026-03-05T22:58 UTC (job-billing-refund-v2). b) Postback replayer processed hour buckets around the swap; ordering of postbacks shows hosted usage postback (edge proxy) arrived before the refund-postback was applied to the hourly accumulator. c) Re-running the replay locally with same ordering reproduced the invoice line behavior. Logs / evidence: - Billing trace: billing.trace/2026-03-05/REF-77 (linked) - Postback timeline: https://internal-logs/redwood/billing/postbacks?org=org-brightlens-77&date=2026-03-05 - Invoice: INV-2026-03-08-ORG77 (screenshot attached by customer) Hypothesis: Out-of-order postback processing caused the hourly accumulator to mark those tokens as hosted at time of final invoice generation before the reserve-refund adjustment was reconciled. Secondary factor: The reserve refund flow should create a retroactive rate-override record for the affected buckets but the override write may have been skipped when hosted postbacks overlapped. Proposed immediate mitigation: create provisional credit equal to the delta and hold autopay; schedule a backfill job to reconcile the hourly accumulator and re-run invoice generation for the affected buckets if needed. Follow-ups: engineering to harden postback ordering guarantees and billing team to add a reconciliation check before invoice finalization.

resolution: Root cause: race condition in postback ordering during partial reserved-hour refund that allowed hosted usage postbacks to be applied before refund adjustment write. Fix: deployed idempotent timestamp gating to hourly accumulator (PR merged 2026-03-11). Remediation: ran accumulator backfill for the affected hour window and issued credit memo CM-2026-03-12-ORG77 for USD 3,600; released autopay hold. Post-actions: billing runbook updated (confluence) to include pre-finalization reconciliation checks; added metric to detect postback ordering anomalies and alerting to #billing-ops. Customer-facing note: Apologized and confirmed credit applied.
